scenario_persistence_override.innovation_formula: eta_d,t = standardize(sum(lambda_d,r * u_r,t) + w_d * epsilon_d,t), with u_r,t root innovations after the current phase root-correlation state and epsilon_d,t the same driver idiosyncratic innovation used by BASE
scenario_persistence_override.initialization: when override begins, y_d,t-1 equals the last emitted standardized driver shock; do not initialize to zero
scenario_persistence_override.ramp_rule: numeric-to-numeric rho is linearly interpolated by phase weight; null is bypass and is not interpreted as rho=0
scenario_persistence_override.validation_rule: on a constant-rho plateau after warm-up, Var(y) must remain approximately 1 and empirical lag-1 correlation must approximate rho; insufficient plateau length is diagnostic, not failure

driver_generation.explicit_idiosyncratic_rule: These taxonomy drivers intentionally have no root mapping in v1.1. They retain independent standardized driver innovations; scenario mean/volatility overrides may still apply if a scenario explicitly names them. No root covariance is implied until a future normative reissue adds a mapping.

scenario.description: US–China semiconductor technology race: Western subsidized capacity buildout, uncertain 3–5Y parity boundary, then persistent bifurcated production systems and accelerator price competition.

probability_meta.rationale: Owner explicitly requested separate probability judgment; calibration must not infer it.

meta.rationale: Scenario is conditioned on an ongoing strategic race at t0.
Western and Chinese fab buildout raises equipment cycle.
Sovereign localization accelerates.
Defense/strategic procurement rises.
AI infrastructure race sustains capex.
Power infrastructure buildout follows compute investment.
Fiscal/industrial investment pressure modestly raises rate environment.
Export controls mildly reduce cross-border addressability.
No physical Taiwan supply impairment is assumed before parity.
Compute service pricing not yet structurally reset.
Competition rises but parity has not yet been reached.
Compute and power buildout become more synchronized.
Capex race depends more on semiconductor supply capability.
Phase 1 encodes the owner thesis of strategic subsidy/capacity race before parity.
Owner thesis explicitly states a 3–5 year lag; triangular q12/q16/q20 encodes that uncertainty without selecting a point estimate.
Both systems accelerate equipment investment around parity.
Western localization response intensifies.
Strategic/defense procurement intensifies.
AI infrastructure spending remains elevated but more volatile.
Power buildout accelerates with duplicated compute systems.
Investment/fiscal intensity raises rate pressure.
Technology/export-control bifurcation reduces cross-border revenue.
Negative shift represents access friction/duplication risk, not loss of Taiwan strategic value.
Cheaper compute begins to pressure service pricing/economics.
Parity sharply increases accelerator price/performance competition.
Duplicated systems tightly couple compute and power investment.
Parity-boundary capex is supply capability dependent.
Technology capability and cross-border market access begin decoupling.
Phase 2 is deliberately volatile and temporary; it is the boundary the owner explicitly asked to study.

phases.name: Persistent Western and Chinese semiconductor systems

meta.rationale: Phase 3 starts after a four-quarter parity-boundary repricing window.
Duplicated supply chains keep equipment demand above BASE.
Strategic localization persists.
Defense/sovereign compute demand remains elevated.
Western AI buildout remains structurally above BASE.
Power infrastructure remains structurally elevated.
Rate pressure moderates but stays above BASE.
Cross-border technology revenue remains structurally impaired.
Supply-access friction remains; driver is not used as a proxy for Taiwan strategic relevance.
Cheaper non-Western chips pressure global compute service economics.
Sustained two-system competition compresses accelerator economics.
Persistent synchronized sovereign compute/power buildout.
Buildout remains supply-capability dependent.
Two production systems can improve local supply health while cross-border market access remains poor.
Persistent bifurcation, not an assumption that either bloc disappears.
